itens: A good Diana player will most likely just sit back and land her Q poke against you without ever commiting towards an all-in,
However: if they are stupid enough to try and walk up for CS:

blocos.texto: Try to time your abilities when they are in the middle of an auto attack animation and then commit towards an all-in.
You should be able to win any extended trade since Diana is so ability-reliant.

itens: Post level 6, this matchup gets even easier for you since you can force the Diana to fight in an extended fight against you with your E -> R combo.

itens: In teamfights, if your team is clumped up together, make sure to ult away the Diana so that her teammates don't have to suffer from a 5-man empowered Diana ultimate.

When Sett is around 25% HP with no W charged up, this is your lethal range to commit towards an all-in with your E -> Q -> W -> Shield bash AA.

Sett's E can only stun you when he has another target to grab on the other side, but fortunately for you: your ultimate can negate that by making it so that the only target he can use his E on is you.
Your ultimate can be canceled by his ultimate assuming he's in melee range from you, so try and ult him from a farther amount of distance to guarantee it.

blocos.texto: NEVER ult him directly in melee range post level 6.

itens: Do not all-in the Sett if he's full hp or near his turret because you will lose a dedicated all-in before you get your dedicated plated steelcaps and level 6 powerspikes.
Be aware that Sett has the ability to insec you into his turret if you overextend too far.

blocos.texto: Don't overextend too far.

itens: If Sett walks up to turret to hit it, don't trade into him too hard without your ultimate because he might be planning on diving you with his ultimate and charged up W.

blocos.texto: Just Q him, and shield bash AA him, and then step back to see what his next move is.
If he dives you, his W shouldn't be charged up enough to kill you.
If he doesn't dive you, wait for his W meter to go back down and poke him down again with your E + AA's.

itens: Level 1, walk with your wave, since some (mentally ill) Shaco players might try to go for a proxy onto you, if they do try to go for it, fight them off.

When the waves meet, you ideally want to fight for priority so that you can crash the third wave for a cheater recall, and subsequently: a rebound back to your turret -> a freeze on your side of the lane.
So long as you can get the Shaco to overextend in your territory, you should be fine to just beat him down whenever he walks up for CS.
Trade for as long as possible against the Shaco until you start to go beyond unmarked and potentially trapped territory.

blocos.texto: The last thing you want to happen against a Shaco player is to get feared by one trap -> feared by another trap -> feared by a recently placed trap, since it will chunk your HP down significantly.

itens: Just try to chip him down with max ranged Q's, and if he ever uses his Q invisibility dash, then look to land your E (ideally while he's trying to use his own E poke onto you)
You should be able to outsustain him as long as you use your W whenever he throws his E knife at you.

Post level 6, when you see Shaco use his ultimate, identify which one is the real Shaco by seeing which one takes more damage from your passive, and then proceed to ult the real Shaco to avoid getting blasted by Shaco's death-clone-damage.

blocos.texto: Bonus points if you can also time your ultimate while you're in an area with a bunch of pre-established traps, since they will not follow him through the death realm.

itens: Be aware of the location of his traps at all times to avoid taking an unnecessary amount of damage.

If you ever see the Shaco randomly use his ultimate, be ESPECIALLY aware of it's timer and existence, since if you don't see it explode, there's a good chance he's going to command his clone to run away, walk towards you, use his Q invisbility, make the clone look like it's him, and then have it explode on top of you for a lot of damage.

blocos.texto: Don't get cheesed.

itens: Don't get rage-baited, I know it's a Shaco, and I KNOW you DESPERATELY want to kill him, but if you're low HP: recall, and don't greed for the kill because you're going to end up looking stupid.
If you're forced to push the wave into him, be sure to walk behind your minions and linearly with your minions so that they can tank any incoming traps.
DO NOT die levels 1-2, these are the only timers where you can lose the Shen player.

blocos.texto: Play respectfully, preserve your HP, let him get priority, and then beat him down level 3 when you have all of your abilities up in a dedicated all-in since Shen is only strong in extremely short trades.
From here, you should push out the wave and recall afterwards for your some items and then play towards your level 6 powerspike.

itens: Before level 3, DO NOT trade into the Shen, you will lose all of your HP and be unable to trade with him afterwards.
Post level 3, try to engage with your E while the Shen is in the middle of an auto attack on the wave.
If the Shen dashes into you with his E, you should try to buffer his taunt with your Q and effectively negate it's CC.
When Shen uses his W (Spirit's Refuge), try to prioritze movement over auto attacking him since he's just going to block it anyways.

blocos.texto: Ideally, try to walk towards wherever his escape-plan could possibly be at.

itens: Like I said before in this entry: DO NOT DIE before level 3, this is the only time when he's stronger than you in combat stats.
Post level 6, PING your teammate's that there's a Shen in the game whenever you don't directly see him in the map.

blocos.texto: And when I say ping: I mean ping in an almost schizophrenic paranoia-induced kind of way:
If you see the man move outside of vision for a split second: ASSUME he's going to be ulting one of his teammates IMMEDIATELY, and make sure your teammate's are blinded by the Shen.
PING, PING, PING!!!!! PLEASE!

itens: Post level 6, you want to try and hold a freeze on your side of the wave for as long as possible.

blocos.texto: If he ever ults out, shove the wave immediately and try to get as many turret plates as possible.
If you're strong enough to contest the enemy jungler, go for a proxy after getting a turret plate and ward the enemy jungle to see if you can maybe snag a camp while you're there.
If you can't, just recall before the Shen comes back, and make use of your tempo advantage to recall and get an additional itemization powerspike.

Against a Shyvana player, you either want to use your ultimate when she's already used hers, while she's in the middle of animation, or when you're out of vision against her,

blocos.texto: Since she'll be able to cancel your ultimate with her ultimate otherwise.

itens: Pay attention to Shyvana's build since an AD shyvana will deal more focused damage against one of your carries and an AP shyvana will deal more AOE damage against your team.

blocos.texto: If it's an AD Shyvana, you don't need to prioritize her nearly as much with your ultimate unless she's actively on one of your carries.
If it's an AP Shyvana however, make sure that you are either positionally seperated by your team so that her R -> E combo doesn't deal massive amounts of AOE damage.

blocos.texto: But: if he's stubborn, he's probably still going to get the wave pushed out and he's probably going to end up going the long way to proxy you.

Just farm under turet until you can get a back timer, get a cull, and then rinse and repeat until you've gotten your Rylai's + Approach Velocity powerspike.

itens: Just stand outside of his purple gas cloud and trade with him for as long as possible until he's too far to continiously prolong a trade without taking an absurd amount of damage from his Q.
When you get your Rylai's + Approach Velocity powerspike, land a Q onto him and trade for as long as possible as per usual.

blocos.texto: If he gets under 50% hp, go for an ult angle and commit towards a longer trade to try and play towards a solokill.

blocos.texto: TRAVERSE REALMS! Which is really annoying because he can still slow you down with glue that looks like it doesn't even exist.

Try to time your E pull during his Q animation to shorten it's duration or straight up cancel it if the Sion doesn't release his Q early.

blocos.texto: From there, just Q him on the head and then run him down until he gets too far away.

itens: Additionally: If you can buffer your Q or your R just when he's about to hit you with his ultimate, you can effectively negate it's CC.

blocos.texto: Also: While it does seem counter productive to ult him while his R is about to hit you, keep in mind that your ultimate has a cast-time, and by ulting him right as he's about to land on top of you, you'll be able to get a successful buffer.

itens: Sion's E shreds your armor, so try to avoid Sion E or any of his abilities that follow up with his Sion E with flash to avoid taking an absurd amount of damage.

itens: Sion's ultimate gives him roaming potential, so just keep that in mind whenever he's not in lane.

blocos.texto: Though, most Sion players just use their ultimate to get back to lane quicker for a tempo advantage.
Just don't be under his turret when you hear his ult sound go off if does use his ultimate for lane.

itens: If you ult Sion while he's charging his Q, and the Sion doesn't cancel his Q early, you can completely negate all the damage you would've gotten because apparently: his Q is left behind in whatever realm he casted it in.

blocos.texto: However, do note that this does mean it's theoretically for one of your teammate's to die from a completely invisible Sion Q.

Unless you overextend into his turret and get insec'd, but at that point, you kind of deserve to die.

itens: Just try to hit him with your E's and Q's whenever he gets into range.
When you see him picking up his Q rock, stand behind minions, but not too close to the minions so that they block the AOE rock throw.
Post level 6 especially: Do not overextend into his side of the lane since there's a good chance he's going to insec you back into his turret and cheese you.

blocos.texto: Just let the wave slowly push back towards you, and you should be fine.

Try to time your E pull for when Smolder goes for a Q or a W onto you and then subsequently chase him down once you've landed your Q to procc your Stromraider's surge.

itens: Soraka's early game is suprisingly oppressive, so just keep playing safe until you get your rocketbelt powerspike into her.
That means giving up level 1 priority, playing safe during the second and third waves, and preserving your HP so that you can play the rebound back to her effectively.
Soraka isn't a matchup you exactly trade with due to her range advantage, but more-so a matchup that you have to survive until you get your tools to properly all-in her.
Once you get your level 6, try to time your E pull for when Soraka walks up to use her Q poke, if you can land everything, you should be able to just kill her in an all-in.
If you can't get into range to land your E, just wait until you get your rocketbelt powerspike to E -> R
> all-in her whenever she's vaguely in range.
Try to use the movement speed gained from Stormraider's surge to charge at the Soraka when you start getting into teamfights to deny her from healing the rest of her team.
When Soraka uses her silence against you, use the movement speed gained from Stormraider's Surge to walk right past it.
Play patient, play safe, and do not underestimate Soraka's lethal ranges.

Level 3, shove the third wave, crash it, and either recall for some items or stay in lane to hold a freeze when the wave inevitably bounces back towards you.

blocos.texto: You can't really force a fight onto him with your E since he can just dash out of it with his E1 (Abscond),

But it's not like he can dash onto you since you can easily just sidestep back into your minions and consequently punish him with your own E and extend said trade towards an all-in since his kit is oriented towards cycling his abilities for burst damage.
Just wait until you get your Dusk & Dawn and then win any fight he takes onto you.

blocos.texto: From here you have three options:

1. Ult someone else so that now, it's a 2v2 in the death realm. 2. Ult the Sylas before he can ult one of your hyper carries so that he's neutralized, you might actually lose the fight now, but at least your hypercarry can still contribute to the fight 3. You kill the Sylas after he leaves your ultimate and give him the PTSD that only Mordekaiser mains know of; being abandoned by your team after you kill someone in your death realm.
But yeah, he's not a hard counter to Mordekaiser because he will almost 100% lose an all-in against you ( unless you ult him first and then he ults you ).

If this is the case, then you can just ult him straight up with no worries.

blocos.texto: And once she gets 120 splinters, her AP has a permanent +15% bonus.
So try and focus immensely on dodging her skillshots if you so happen to get hit by one to delay her 120 splinter powerspike for as long as possible.

Make sure to position your ultimate in a way where he can't just flip over a wall and escape you entirely.

itens: Taric genuinely has terrifying all-in potential until you've gotten some sort of anti-healing to cut down his sustain.
Give up level 1 priority, and play exclusively towards short trading with him.
Level 2, level up your W and only fight him with your Q's and shield bash auto attacks.
Level 3 is when the wave is going to start slowly rebounding towards him, assuming you let the wave push towards you, make sure your HP is high so that you can effectively secure the crash.

blocos.texto: Keep playing safe until you've gotten Oblivion Orb, and once you've gotten that powerspike, you can expand your trade durations a little bit to make him use more of his mana.

itens: Before you get your oblivion orb, the only trades you want to be doing against him are max range Q's, and shield bash procc's if he ever gets too close.

blocos.texto: Trading with him long in the early game is a generally bad idea since he'll just be able to out-sustain you.

itens: Once you do get your oblivion orb powerspike, you can start prolonging trades until your W shield gets low to make him use more of his mana on healing himself with his Q.

blocos.texto: If he gets low enough for an all-in to kill him (around 30% HP) or if he runs out mana, prolong the trade.

itens: Follow the same philosophy once you get your ultimate.
In teamfights, make sure to ult away the Taric when he starts to use his ultimate so that your team doesn't have to deal with a bunch of invulnerable enemies.
Do not underestimate Taric's all-in pressure early game despite him being a support champion. It is deceptively strong.

Then: just rebound the wave, and then either recall for health or stay in lane to not miss EXP.

You will die.

itens: Tryndamere, with grasp or hail of blades or lethal tempo is always going to be EXTREMELY scary when you fight him close-range.

blocos.texto: Give up level 2 priority, stay behind minions, and poke him down when he overextends onto you.
When the wave gets your turret, play for the rebound and slowly push it out while continously poking the Tryndamere as you slowly push out.
Afterwards, get a recall off, and get your Warden's Mail / Plated Steelcaps components (Dealer's choice).
You'll still probably not be able to beat him when you do get Warden's Mail / plated steelcaps in an all-in, but it does help with giving you a little bit more time to stall out his ultimate.

itens: Ideally try to stand outside of his auto attack range and force him to use his E spin against you if he ever wants to trade with you.
If he doesn't spin onto you, keep playing the neutral game and keep repeatedly poking him with your Q's over and over again.
If Tryndamere does spin on you, use your W, procc your grasp + shield bash ontohim with an auto attack, and then E him away to then Q him on the head.

blocos.texto: You never want to play fair; only play towards short trades until he's really low HP (30% hp), AND you have exhaust.

If he's in lethal range, try to time your E when he's in the middle of his auto attack animation (or if he's already used it), exhaust him when he's in range and pray that you have enough damage to get him to use his ultimate early.
If you can get him to use his ultimate early, run and stall for at long as possible: but not too far in case you can potentially snag a kill against him.
If you're successful in surviving, you can walk back and finish him off with a Q onto the head.

itens: Be exceptionally aware of what runes the Tryndamere is going since it will determine the amount of leniency you have when it comes to the duration of trades.

blocos.texto: Grasp Tryndamere is only useful for the initial auto attack and should be traded with a little bit longer with your shield bash and passive before backing off.
Hail Of Blades Tryndamere requires you to keep the trade as short as physically possible to avoid tanking a potential triple crit combo IF he has a high amount of fury.
If he doesn't have a high amount of fury, you can afford to extend a trade a little bit longer, so long as he's engaging on your side of the wave.
And finally: Lethal Tempo Tryndamere requires you to exclusively play for short trades unless you know for sure that you can get a quick lethal procc against him.
If a lethal tempo tryndamere uses his ultimate against you, use your E to force him off and do not engage him until his ultimate is just about to run out

itens: Try to ult the Tryndamere when he's at lower HP so that you can yoink more AD.
In the mid game, try to keep lanes pushed out before teamfights so he cannot splitpush and destroy your entire base for free.

blocos.texto: (Which you should only go for if you have warden's mail) Just be sure to step to the side in case he goes for this play.

blocos.texto: Meaning: you want to try and prolong trades against her for as long as possible after negating her Q damage while the wave is on your side of the lane.
Now: this can be done with one of two ways:

itens: You can either dodge it with good movement or with flash,
or you can cancel her Q dash with your E.

blocos.texto: Either way: you should be able be able to land an E pull and then extend said trade to your heart's content since a majority of her trade patterns from rapid instances of burst damage.

itens: If Vi is not using her Q against you, she'll most likely poke you out with her E AOE damage,

blocos.texto: Just wait for her to use her ultimate first,

itens: A majority of the time when you're trading against Viego, you want to try and focus more-so on avoiding his trade patterns instead of creating your own.

itens: Before level 6, you can more accurately land your E pulls if you can time it when Viego is in the middle of his empowered auto animations or while he's in the middle of channeling his W, which slows him down by 10%.

blocos.texto: Alternatively, you can also just wait for him to use his ultimate first.

itens: If one of your teammates die outside of your death realm, and Viego got an assist on them, he can possess said teammate, get a second of invulnerability, a bunch of HP back, and a refund on his ultimate.

itens: You can theoretically get more stats if you ult Viego while he's inside of his E shroud, but honestly: just keep ulting him while he's channeling his W animation to avoid the risk of getting your ultimate canceled.
